verbalization: Chloroprocaine is implicated in the pathogenesis of Pseudocholinesterase Deficiency, a condition caused by the enzymatic inactivation of procaine by pseudocholinesterase. This relationship is mediated through the interaction of procaine with Slc6a3, suggesting a potential mechanism by which chloroprocaine influences the expression or function of the Slc6a3 transporter. The lowest common ancestor of Chloroprocaine and Procaine points to Benzoate Ester and Anesthetic Agent, indicating a shared biochemical pathway involving esterification and anesthetic effects. The evidence suggests that chloroprocaine may indirectly affect Slc6a3 through its role in procaine metabolism, highlighting a complex interplay between anesthetic agents and transporter function. The relationship is supported by the observed binding of procaine to Slc6a3, implying a possible regulatory role of procaine in the activity of the Slc6a3 transporter.
